text:
maria: Quick perf heads-up: noticed a big spike in CPU wakeups on gtx-srv-07 during the 10k qps run. nsys GPU timeline looks fine but CPU-side perf/flame shows tokenization + scheduler spinning a lot :eyes:

jon: ah, saw that in the nightly perf traces too. summary from my local run: lots of irq/futex wakeups, and the batcher thread is repeatedly waking then sleeping. could be interrupt coalescing + timer granularity interaction.

maria: exact symptoms: bursts of 40-60k wakeups/min around peak, latency p95 jumps ~2x. KV cache hit distribution unchanged. suspect the batcher wait heuristic (we wait on cond var with 1ms timeouts) interacting badly with NIC coalescing.

tk: can you paste the perf capture command you used? want to reproduce on a dev box.

jon: sure — what i ran:```sudo perf record -F 200 -g -a -- sleep 30``` then```perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded; ./flamegraph.pl out.folded > perf.svg``` the flame shows a big wedge from `pthread_cond_timedwait` -> `batcher::wait` -> `py::tokenize` and another from `hrtimer`/`irq` -> `softirq_processing` -> `net_rx`.

maria: i also did a perf top: top entries were `tokenizer::split_and_norm`, `batcher::drain`, `pthread_cond_wait`, and `__do_softirq`. Notably, `memcpy` in kv lookup showed up but was small relative to wakeup cost.

sree: interesting. hardware-level coalescing may be batching interrupts into bursts that align with our cond wait wakeups. When NIC flush hits, kernel sends softirq(s) and timers wake the batcher, causing repeated short run/sleep cycles. Did you check `dmesg` for irq balance churn?

maria: looked at irqaffinity + irqbalance logs — irqbalance did a few reassigns during the run but not many. Also tried toggling `net.core.netdev_max_backlog` and `rx-usecs` (coalescing) in a staging run: increasing `rx-usecs` from 0 -> 50 reduced wakeups by ~30% and smoothed p99 latency.

tk: nice. That suggests two short-term mitigations: 1) increase interrupt coalescing on NIC to reduce wakeup frequency, 2) change batcher heuristic from strict 1ms timed wait to adaptive exponential backoff when QPS below threshold.

jon: agree. For longer term we should: - add a perf harness that records both `perf` and `trace-cmd`/ftrace for softirq/wakeup paths - instrument batcher to emit micro-metrics (sleep durations, wake counts) - evaluate using `timerfd` with coalescing-friendly flags or `pthread_cond_wait` without spin if low QPS.

maria: i've attached the tiny snippet i used to toggle coalescing:```# echo 50 > /sys/class/net/eth0/queues/rx-0/rx-usecs``` on our test VMs. Also turned off `CONFIG_PREEMPT` in one kernel variant to see effects — that reduced scheduler wake churn but increased tail latency in other paths (expected).

perf-bot: Perf capture summary for 2091112222 run: samples=182k, user=62%, kernel=28%, idle-wakeup: 43k, top stacks: batcher::wait -> pthread_cond_wait (18%), softirq/net_rx -> ksoftirqd (14%), tokenizer::* (12%).

sree: next steps: can someone put together a small reproducer that toggles `rx-usecs` and batcher timeout in a controlled harness (maybe use wrk to generate steady ramp)? i'll take the profiler + ftrace side.

maria: i'll add a minimal harness in infra/perf-harness and run controlled tests. i'll paste the perf.svg and a short flame snapshot once done. also adding a quick check to the batcher that logs when we get >10 wakeups/sec outside active streams.

jon: SGTM. one more note — kernel tickless (`NO_HZ_FULL`) sometimes changes behavior; we should try with/without to see if it reduces periodic timer noise.

maria: good call. thanks all — will post results in this thread when i have the harness output and the flamegraph. :thumbsup:
